summary: Eight-band parametric EQ, minimum phase and zero latency (Phase Linear: the same response as one linear-phase filter, 4607 samples late, with a 32-point Curve layer): bell, low and high shelf, low and high cut at 12/24/48 dB/oct, notch; frequency in Hz, gain in 0.1 dB steps, Q. Bands 2–7 start on at 0 dB (transparent until a gain is set); the cuts, bands 1 and 8, start off. Use it for precise, labelled moves such as "B3: Bell, 320 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1.4". Mode Graphic makes it a 31-band graphic EQ at the ISO third-octave centres (G 20 Hz … G 20 kHz, ±18 dB in 0.1 dB steps) whose response passes through its sliders: for a curve given band by band, such as "G 125 Hz −3 dB, G 4 kHz +2 dB". v2: each band on Stereo, Left, Right, Mid or Side; shapes (proportional-Q bell, Baxandall and Vintage shelves, all-pass); dynamic bands (gain down or up above a threshold, the detector on the band's own shape or on the sidechain, input 2), e.g. "B5: Bell, 6.5 kHz, Side, dynamic Down, threshold −30 dB, range 6 dB" to tame sibilance; Delta, and the gain-match reading.
use_for: Eight-band parametric EQ for corrective cuts and broad tone shaping, minimum or linear phase.

parameters.name: B1 on
parameters.description: Band 1 in or out (an off band passes the signal untouched)
parameters.how: Switches band 1 in or out; an off band passes the signal untouched.
parameters.sound: On, band 1's shape is applied; off, the sound is unchanged by it.

parameters.name: B1 type
parameters.description: Band 1: bell, shelves (half the gain at the frequency), Butterworth cuts (−3 dB at the frequency with Q 0.71), notch
parameters.how: Chooses band 1's shape: bell, low shelf, high shelf, low cut, high cut or notch.
parameters.sound: Bells boost or cut one region, shelves tilt the lows or highs, cuts remove the extremes and a notch carves a narrow hole.

parameters.name: B1 freq
parameters.description: Band 1 frequency: centre, shelf midpoint or cutoff
parameters.how: Sets band 1's frequency, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz: its centre, shelf midpoint or cutoff.
parameters.sound: Moving it chooses which part of the sound the band shapes, from deep bass to air.

parameters.name: B1 gain
parameters.description: Band 1 gain in 0.1 dB steps (bells and shelves)
parameters.how: Sets band 1's boost or cut, from -24 to +24 dB, for bells and shelves.
parameters.sound: Positive values bring that region forward; negative values pull it back.

parameters.name: B1 Q
parameters.description: Band 1 Q: bell and notch width, shelf and cut resonance (0.71 is flat)
parameters.how: Sets band 1's width, from 0.1 to 30; higher values are narrower (and make shelves and cuts resonate).
parameters.sound: Narrow values shape one tone or resonance; wide values change the broad tone smoothly.

parameters.name: B1 slope
parameters.description: Band 1 slope (low and high cut)
parameters.how: Sets the steepness of band 1 when it is a low or high cut: 12, 24 or 48 dB per octave.
parameters.sound: Steeper slopes remove the cut region more completely; gentler ones blend in more naturally.

parameters.name: B1 channel
parameters.description: Band 1: which channel it works on. Stereo: both (as v1); Left or Right: that one alone; Mid or Side: the mid (L+R)/2 or the side (L−R)/2 alone, the other untouched (mid/side encoded and decoded around the band)
parameters.how: Chooses which channel band 1 works on: both, left, right, mid or side.
parameters.sound: Mid or side lets you shape the centre or the width alone, for example brightening only the sides.

parameters.name: B1 shape
parameters.description: Band 1: Standard: the type as it is (as v1). Proportional Q: a bell narrows as its gain grows (Q × 10^(|gain|/40): about twice as narrow for every 12 dB). Baxandall: a shelf becomes first order, 6 dB/oct, the gentle tone-control curve (Q unused). Vintage: a shelf gets its complementary dip, Pultec-style: a bell of half its gain the other way, Q 1, an octave above a low shelf or below a high shelf. All-pass: whatever the type, the band only turns the phase (second order at its frequency, Q its width)
parameters.how: Chooses band 1's character: Standard, Proportional Q, Baxandall, Vintage or All-pass.
parameters.sound: Proportional Q narrows with gain for a more musical feel, Baxandall makes a gentle tone-control tilt and All-pass shifts phase without changing tone.

parameters.name: B1 dynamic
parameters.description: Band 1 dynamic EQ (bells and shelves): Down: above the threshold the band's gain moves down (compresses what it hears), Up: it moves up; by the ratio, at most Range. The detector hears the band's own shape (a band-pass for a bell, low-pass for a low shelf, high-pass for a high shelf). Off: static (as v1)
parameters.how: Makes band 1 dynamic: Down turns its gain down when its detector gets loud, Up turns it up.

parameters.description: Hear only what the EQ changes: the output minus the input, before Output (zero latency, nothing to delay), gliding over 10 ms. Off for rendering
parameters.how: Plays only the difference between the output and the input.
parameters.sound: You hear only what the EQ adds or removes.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Minimum: the bands as always, zero latency. Linear: one FIR from the bands' zero-phase magnitude (same dB at every frequency from 30 Hz, no phase turning, constant delay of 4095 + 512 samples at 44.1/48 kHz, reported to the host); Parametric mode only; dynamic bands are static in it; the Curve layer applies; a very narrow band at a low frequency is limited in Q (the editor says so)
parameters.how: Chooses minimum phase with no latency, or linear phase with a constant delay of about 4600 samples (about 100 ms).
parameters.sound: Linear phase keeps the timing of all frequencies intact, which sounds cleaner on big boosts and in mastering.
